questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Count rate from a beta source with a known efficiency
questions.learningObjective: Find emitted rate from count rate
questions.stem: Detector reads 2000 s^-1 at efficiency 0.05; emitted beta rate?
questions.explanation: Emitted = counts / efficiency = 2000 / 0.05 = 40000 s^-1. Multiplying gives 100, too low.

questions.subject: PHYSICS_I
questions.topic: Why a beta decay often leaves an excited daughter nucleus
questions.learningObjective: Explain energy sharing in beta decay
questions.stem: Explain why beta decay energy is shared among products.

answer.exemplar: The decay energy is shared as kinetic energy among the beta particle, the antineutrino, and sometimes recoil. This variable sharing produces a continuous beta energy spectrum.

questions.explanation: Three products share the energy, so the beta particle energy varies continuously. A two-body decay would give a fixed energy.

questions.topic: Direction of a beta particle in crossed fields
questions.learningObjective: Determine sense of beta curvature
questions.stem: A beta particle curves clockwise as seen from above; B field points

options.misconception: B must be vertical for this view

questions.explanation: For a negative charge to curve clockwise viewed from above, the B field points downward. Upward field would curve counterclockwise.
